title: Agro-Ecological Crop Planning, Seasonal Rotations and Risk Management
crop: Soybean, Cotton, Gram/Chickpea, Wheat, Jowar, Tur/Pigeonpea
source_name: Department of Agriculture, Govt of Maharashtra & MPKV Rahuri Agronomy Division
summary: Scientific crop rotation prevents soil exhaustion, breaks pest life-cycles, improves water-use efficiency, and diversifies farm income.
content: Recommended Crop Rotations for Maharashtra: 1) Soybean - Chickpea (हरभरा): Best for assured rainfall zones in Marathwada/Vidarbha. Soybean matures in 90-100 days (leaving residual moisture and nitrogen), followed immediately by zero-till or minimum-till Desi Chickpea (Vijay / Digvijay variety) or Kabuli Chickpea (PKV 2 / Kripa). 2) Cotton + Pigeonpea (कापूस + तूर): Intercropping system 6:1 or 8:1 row ratio. Pigeonpea roots break hardpan and fix atmospheric nitrogen; acts as biological barrier. 3) Bajra - Mustard / Chickpea: For dryland light soils in Ahmednagar, Solapur, Beed. Requires minimal water. 4) Sugarcane - Intercropping: Intercrop onion, potato, or groundnut during first 75 days of sugarcane to generate cash flow and utilize vacant inter-row space. Factors in Selection: A) Water Availability: If winter well recharge is low, choose low-water Chickpea (needs 2-3 irrigations) instead of Wheat (needs 5-6 irrigations). B) Soil Depth: Shallow soils (<30 cm) suitable for Bajra, Moong, Udid; Medium-deep soils (30-90 cm) for Soybean, Cotton, Jowar; Deep black soils (>90 cm) for Wheat, Sugarcane, Gram. C) Market access: High perishable vegetables need APMC road connectivity within 50 km.
